summary: SelectionInfo dataclass plus the hit-policy selection layer (collect/unique/first/priority/any/rule_order) over survivor frames: ordering_keys/default_output_fields for ordering and output-field resolution, check_policy_config/check_priority for pre-scoring configuration validation, check_assertions/apply_cardinality for UNIQUE/ANY assertions and cardinality truncation, plus new normalize_policy/validate_priority_field/validate_output_fields input guards, selection_is_truncated for conservative re-selection safety, and first_per_context for batch best-match selection.
lifecycle_notes: The six hit policies existed at the accepted baseline; this refresh adds explicit schema validation and conservative selection-completeness tracking.

SelectionInfo gained a 'metadata_backed: bool = False' field; default_output_fields() now raises ValueError('hit_policy=any requires explicit output_fields without metadata') when output_fields is empty and metadata_backed is False, instead of silently returning no output columns.
normalize_policy(policy) added: coerces a HitPolicy|str via HitPolicy(policy) and raises ValueError('Invalid hit policy: ...') for anything else, replacing a previous implicit fallthrough.

validate_priority_field permits None but rejects other non-string or empty values. validate_output_fields rejects non-string, empty, duplicate or unknown field names; an empty sequence itself is permitted, with policy-specific requirements enforced separately.

selection_info_from_metadata(): priority_field resolution changed from 'priority_field or md_priority' (falsy fallback, so an explicit empty-string priority_field was silently ignored) to 'priority_field if priority_field is not None else md_priority' followed by validate_priority_field() — an explicit empty string now raises instead of silently deferring to metadata. It also gained a keyword-only 'output_fields: tuple[str, ...] = ()' parameter used only when metadata is None, and dimensions with match_strategy == MatchStrategy.CONTEXT_REGEX are now excluded from dimension_rule_fields (a CONTEXT_REGEX dimension has no per-rule resolved_rule_field; it is a global context validator, per compiler.py's _compile_context_regex).

check_policy_config rejects missing PRIORITY fields and invalid ANY output configuration before scoring, including on empty input. check_priority separately rejects null priorities on surviving rules; rejected rules do not trigger that value check.

check_assertions()'s ANY branch now calls default_output_fields(rel.columns, info) unconditionally (previously only when rel.count_rows() > 1), so a metadata-less ANY policy without output_fields now raises regardless of survivor count, not only when more than one rule survives.

selection_is_truncated(policy, top_n, min_specificity) added: conservative truncation predicate (true for FIRST/PRIORITY/ANY or when top_n/min_specificity is set) used by result.py's select() to mark a just-reselected RuleResult as truncated for any further select() calls.

first_per_context(rel) added: group_by('__context_id').agg(min('__rank')) then inner-join back on ['__context_id', '__rank'] — used by batch_result.py's best_matches instead of a bare '__rank == 1' filter, so it no longer assumes rank 1 survives for every context.
risks: selection_is_truncated() is a static predicate over policy/top_n/min_specificity; it does not inspect the actual result size, so a FIRST/PRIORITY/ANY selection over a single-survivor set is still conservatively marked truncated even though no information was actually lost.
